# dsh-app-usage
Local session statistics with a per-provider breakdown (activity heatmap panel).

A DeepSeek Harness plugin,
packaged as a DSH bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and

`cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `app-usage` row into the active profile.
The client half is served f
rom `lib/client.js` (`dsh.client.platform: web`).
## Install

- Desktop app: **Plugins** → install `github:bosenok/dsh-app-usage` (private repository:
give the ma

chine git access), then enable the bundle.
- CLI: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:bosenok

/dsh-app-usage`.
- Local checkout: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:/path/to/dsh-app-usage`.

Enabling the bundle mounts the plugin; HMR applies it to a running app, and a
restart makes sure the
client half is rebuilt.

> Note for the app-managed `desktop` profile: `dsh plugin --profile desktop add`
> only installs the

dependency and copies the package; unlike a regular profile
> it does not enable the bundle. Enable

it by adding the package name to
> `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json`

(or through the
> Plugins page). Other profiles enable the installed bundle automatically.
## Versioning

This project follows Semantic Versioning (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`).
Releases are tagged in git (`v0.1.0`

and later `v0.1.x` tags), announced
as GitHub releases and documented in CHANGELOG.md.
`engines.dsh` in `package.json` pins the compatible DSH range.

Bump policy: **patch** — fixes; **minor** — new features without breaking the
configuration; **major

** — breaking changes to the configuration, the session
format or the supported DSH range.
